final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more carefully. That reframing is valid as a critique of the earlier overbroad certification theory, but it does not satisfy the underlying compliance predicate. The current evidence still shows a material limitation affecting a named launch use case, while policy requires such a limitation to be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. None of those conditions is evidenced here. A caveated statement that certification could proceed only if one of those policy paths is completed is not the same as evidence that the present record is compliant. The narrowed position is therefore analytically better but still insufficient for compliant_with_caveats on the current record, because the caveat identifies an unresolved requirement rather than a satisfied condition with minor qualifications.
remaining_concerns: The loan modification support segment is a named launch use case in two lender rollout commitments and still misses target by 1.4 percentage points.
Policy treats weaknesses affecting a named launch use case as material; the 7% non-core framing does not resolve materiality.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed in launch documentation.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering launch without disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows remediation and re-evaluation to target before launch.
Legal review remains open, so the nondisclosure theory is contested rather than established.
General public guidance on monitoring and model-card documentation does not satisfy the policy-required path for a material limitation.
